record.paper_title: Open problems in local discrete holomorphic dynamics
record.original_question: For a non-invertible dominant germ f in End(C^3, O), under what conditions does there exist a modification π: M̃ → C^3 based at the origin, a point p in the exceptional fiber π^{-1}(O), and a holomorphic germ f̃ in End(M̃, p) that is rigid or at least weakly rigid and satisfies π ◦ f̃ = f ◦ π?

evidence.quote: (OP12) Under which conditions on f ∈ End(C^3, O) there exist a modification π: M˜ → C^3 based at O, a point p ∈ E = π^{-1}(O) and a (possibly weakly) rigid holomorphic germ f˜ ∈ End(M˜, p) so that π ◦ f˜ = f ◦ π?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathrm{End}(\mathbb{C}^n, O)$ denote the set of holomorphic germs $f:(\mathbb{C}^n, O) \to (\mathbb{C}^n, O)$ fixing the origin. A germ $f$ is called dominant if its Jacobian determinant is not identically zero, and non-invertible if $df_O$ is singular. A modification based at $O$ is a proper holomorphic map $\pi: \widetilde{M} \to \mathbb{C}^n$ that is a biholomorphism off the exceptional fiber $E = \pi^{-1}(O)$, with $\widetilde{M}$ a smooth complex manifold. For a holomorphic germ $g \in \mathrm{End}(\widetilde{M}, p)$, the generalized critical set is the union of the irreducible hypersurface germs at $p$ contained in some iterated critical set of $g$. The germ $g$ is called rigid if its generalized critical set is a (possibly empty) divisor with simple normal crossings at $p$ that is totally invariant under $g$, and weakly rigid if the same holds after allowing the divisor to have normal crossings only generically (in a suitable weakened sense).

Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on a non-invertible dominant germ $f \in \mathrm{End}(\mathbb{C}^3, O)$ under which there exist:
\begin{itemize}
\item a modification $\pi: \widetilde{M} \to \mathbb{C}^3$ based at $O$,
\item a point $p \in E = \pi^{-1}(O)$,
\item a holomorphic germ $\widetilde{f} \in \mathrm{End}(\widetilde{M}, p)$ which is rigid (or at least weakly rigid),
\end{itemize}
satisfying the semi-conjugacy relation $\pi \circ \widetilde{f} = f \circ \pi$.
artifact.status_search_result: Rigidification has been established in dimension two (Favre–Jonsson and subsequent work, including the general non-invertible case treated in arXiv:0911.4023), but a corresponding rigidification theorem for dominant non-invertible germs in dimension three is not known. No published resolution of the three-dimensional case was located, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Rigidification of holomorphic germs with non-invertible differential
status_evidence.snippet: Treats rigidification for germs (C^2,0) -> (C^2,0) with non-invertible differential by blow-ups, providing a rigid lifting; results stated in dimension two.
status_evidence.claim: Rigidification is established in dimension two; the three-dimensional analogue is not addressed there.
